title: Preflight failures send the RPC URL with its API key to the Telegram chat and the fatal log: the failure reason embeds the ethers error message, which for HTTP-level RPC errors includes info.requestUrl (reproduced offline)

evidence.note: checkWalletBalance catch: reason and details.err embed err.message
preflight(): log.fatal with reason + details, then sendTelegramAlert(`*PREFLIGHT FATAL* [...] ${r.reason}`)

evidence.ref: node rpc-reason-repro.js (scratch folder outside the repo (Node 22.16.0; no src/ import, no .env, no live DB; loopback 127.0.0.1 only); ethers 6.16.0 from the repo; loopback JSON-RPC server answering eth_chainId then HTTP 500; fake API key in the URL path)
evidence.note: output: code SERVER_ERROR; reason contains key: true; message ends with info={ "requestUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v2/<KEY>", ... }

sibling_sites_checked: Every preflight check that wraps an RPC error: checkWalletBalance (:220-232), checkEntryExitAffordability (:462-477, reason returned to bot.ts and logged), checkRpcChainId (:498-506), checkRpcBlockAge (:538-545), checkMevHealth (:575-582), checkHoneypotCheckerCode (:613-620). Only preflight() forwards reasons to Telegram (:986-990); the mid-run wallet check reuses checkWalletBalance (bot.ts, BUY slice). Hosted RPC URLs carry the key in the path (.env.example:13, :54).
severity_rationale: S2 EXPOSURE: on an RPC provider outage or rate limit at boot (ordinary), the provider API key is sent to Telegram servers and the chat history, in addition to the logs (AUD-TX-014 covers the log sink in the TX slice). No funds move with an RPC key; a leaked key can be abused against the operator account.
recommendation: Build preflight reasons from error.code and a masked host only (api/routes/chains.ts already has maskUrl), never err.message; with card TX-04, check the Telegram chat history and rotate the RPC key if a FATAL reason ever contained it.
